correctness.rationale: Complete 1-types over the homogeneous poset correspond bijectively to order-ideal/order-filter pairs with all lower-to-upper comparisons; in height two this yields t(A)=2|J(A)|-1+B(A). The symmetric 2-by-2 transfer matrix gives the crown ideal count and, upon forbidding a chord, an exact Fibonacci product deficit. The even-index Lucas identity and endpoint correction prove strict one-chord recovery. A separate split-path partition calculation gives identical ideals for two nonisomorphic two-chord families for all n>=5; common-upper-neighborhood contributions coincide. Degree/common-neighbor invariants certify nonisomorphism; n=3 chord symmetry and n=4 explicit 16-subset enumeration establish sharpness. The independent executable checker confirms the stated bounded examples, and is not substituted for the all-size proof.

value.rationale: The one-point type count is a natural invariant of finite named parameter spaces in the generic poset. For perturbations of the same canonical crown, it reconstructs the unique chord displacement exactly, but adding only one more comparison can destroy injectivity even with equal cardinality and degree data. A proved infinite twin family plus the smallest possible eight-parameter example gives a structural and sharp information-loss boundary. This is not a stand-alone arithmetic substitution or unsupported application claim.
